payload.body: The chroma filterbank is a fixed 12×N transformation matrix that folds a frequency spectrum into 12 pitch-class bins. Its parameters are: (1) N, the number of frequency bins in the input spectrum (matching the FFT size), (2) the 12 pitch-class center frequencies (typically derived from the equal-tempered scale at 440 Hz reference), and (3) the window function applied to each bin (commonly Gaussian or triangular). The persistence mechanism is the fixed mathematical mapping: for each frame, the filterbank multiplies the spectral vector by the 12×N matrix, summing energy at all frequencies that harmonically correspond to each of the 12 pitch classes (C through B). This produces the octave-invariant chroma vector. The filterbank itself — distinct from the chroma vector it produces — is the transformation kernel, stored as a fixed weight matrix in MIR toolkits (Librosa, Essentia). payload.body: Spectral-band-crossover is a spectral analysis parameter indicating the frequency within a defined sub-band at which the cumulative energy reaches 50% of the band's total energy — the band-local median frequency. Parameters: (1) the band's lower and upper frequency bounds, (2) the spectral energy values across frequency bins within the band. Computed by sorting frequency bins in ascending order by frequency, accumulating energy until the accumulated total reaches half the band's total energy; the frequency at that point is the crossover point. Distinct from spectral-band-centroid (weighted mean, sensitive to energy outliers) and spectral-band-rolloff (arbitrary threshold like 85%, indicating brightness); the crossover is the energy-median, robust to heavy-tailed distributions. Displayed as a scalar time series over analysis frames. [formal: centrum medium spectrale | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.body: Spectral-band-variance is a spectral analysis parameter quantifying the dispersion of spectral energy within a defined frequency sub-band of a spectrum at a given analysis frame. It is the band-localized (second-moment) statistic of the spectral-band moment family, computed from the per-bin energy values inside the band. It measures how spread out the energy is across the band's bins: a concentrated band (one dominant bin) has low band-variance, an evenly spread band has high.
